text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former president Kenneth Kaunda has admitted to meeting the head of South Africa's Armscor weapons firm during a recent visit to Johannesburg, but denied that he was plotting to overthrow the Lusaka government.
- Civic leaders condemned skirmishes between supporters of the government and the opposition.
- Former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party says it has not paid some 400 workers their salaries for 12 months, because it is broke.
- Some 700 secondary school pupils in the southern town of Choma rioted over bad meals in the school dining hall.
- Witnesses in a case in which two businessmen face fraud charges said President Frederick Chiluba owed a maize supplier 61 million kwacha ($65,000).
- The ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy's Lusaka leadership has urged reporters to stop covering rallies called by Kaunda.
- Public servants' unions say they plan industrial action to force the government to give them more pay.
